title: test(spec): export-surface pins compare a build-time baseline instead of running tsc (#4796)
body:
Fixes #4796 — direction 2, the half the card stayed open for after both stop-the-bleed laps landed (PR #4856, then PR #4864).

Seventeen pin tests across thirteen files answered the same question — *which source declaration does entry point X export under name Y?* — and each answered it by building its **own** `ts.createProgram` over all sixteen entry points and running `getTypeChecker()` inside a vitest `it()`. That resolution is now a checked-in artifact, `packages/spec/export-origins/<entry>.json`, and the pins compare against it.

## Re-enumerated on this base

The card's list of 12 files was a lead, not a fact — it was **18** by the time this branch forked, and the three classes are not the same problem:

| class | files | what it does | in scope |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **A — export-surface resolution** | 13 files / **17 cases** | `createProgram` over *every entry point* + `getTypeChecker` → export names and declaration origins | ✅ converted |
| **B — type-shape channel** | `data/driver.test.ts`, `ui/app.test.ts` | `createProgram` over *one file*, asserts a retired key is **unwritable in the authored type** | ❌ different fact — see below |
| **C — TSDoc channel** | `contracts/sharing-service.test.ts` (×4) | `createSourceFile` — a syntactic parse, no program, no checker | ❌ costs nothing |

Class B is not a gap I skipped quietly: "is this property writable in the authored type" is not an export origin, and no export-surface baseline can carry it. Both cases stay exactly as they were, and `vitest.config.ts`'s `testTimeout` comment now says so, so the next reader is not left wondering why `grep typescript` still finds hits.

### The 17 converted pins

| # | file | pin |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | `api/rest-server.test.ts` | `resolves the export surface: no public entry names any of the six` |
| 2 | `automation/state-machine.test.ts` | `…: no entry but ./kernel declares EventSchema` |
| 3 | `automation/sync-retirement.test.ts` | `…: one owner per name, across every public entry` |
| 4 | `cloud/tenant.test.ts` | `…: only ./cloud declares TenantPlan(Schema)…` |
| 5 | `integration/connector.test.ts` | `no name resolves to two declarations across ./shared and ./integration` |
| 6 | `integration/connector.test.ts` | `…across ./shared, ./integration and ./data` |
| 7 | `kernel/activation-events-retirement.test.ts` | `…: the retired names have ZERO holders…` |
| 8 | `kernel/package-dependency-dual-source.test.ts` | `…: one owner per name, across every public entry` |
| 9 | `kernel/plugin-runtime-retirement.test.ts` | `…: the retired names have ZERO holders…` |
| 10 | `studio/action-location-retirement.test.ts` | `…: one owner per name, across every public entry` |
| 11 | `system/environment-artifact.test.ts` | `…: one declaration in ./system, ./cloud re-exports it…` |
| 12 | `system/notification.test.ts` | `…: no removed name survives on any entry…` |
| 13 | `ui/interaction-config-retirement.test.ts` | `every retired name has ZERO holders on any public entry` |
| 14 | `ui/notification-embed-retirement.test.ts` | `…: the retired names have ZERO holders…` |
| 15 | `ui/view.test.ts` | `both entry points resolve the TYPE to the one declaration in shared/http.zod.ts` |
| 16 | `ui/view.test.ts` | `…: ./ui has no HttpMethod, ./shared and ./api share one` |
| 17 | `ui/widget-i18n-retirement.test.ts` | `every retired name has ZERO holders on any public entry` |

## Old pin → new pin, one for one

Every assertion that existed has a successor that fails under the same condition. The conversion is deliberately mechanical: the testkit exposes the same three primitives the pins built by hand, so the assertion bodies carry over rather than being rewritten.

| the retired in-test call | its successor | claim |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `Object.keys(entries)` (built from `package.json`'s exports map) | `EXPORT_ENTRY_POINTS` | identical — the generator reads the same map with the same filter |
| `expect(Object.keys(entries).length).toBeGreaterThan(10)` | same, plus the generator **and** the testkit each refuse below the floor | tighter — the anti-vacuity floor is now enforced three times, once where the artifact is written |
| `expect(moduleSym).toBeTruthy()` | generator **throws** on an unresolvable module symbol | tighter — a resolution failure can no longer be written down and handed to 17 pins |
| `exportsOf(sub).map(e => e.getName())` | `exportNamesOf(entry)` | identical |
| `originOf(sym, label)` → `<file>:<line>` | `originOf(entry, name)` → `<file>#<declared name> (<kind>)` | identical as an **identity** (equal ⇔ same declaration) |
| `expect(origin).toMatch(/^src\/x\.zod\.ts:\d+$/)` | `expect(originFileOf(entry, name)).toBe('src/x.zod.ts')` | **tighter** — the line was matched as `\d+`, i.e. never; the file is now exact |
| local `holdersOf(name) → string[]` | `holdersOf(name)` | identical |
| local `holdersOf(name) → {sub, origin}[]` | `holderOriginsOf(name)` | identical |
| the per-entry `Map<name, origin>` built by hand | `originMapOf(entry)` | identical — the conflict pins' set algebra is unchanged |
| `for (sub of entries) … expect(origin).toBe(canonical)` | `expect(originsOf(name)).toEqual([canonical])` | identical — one distinct origin across all entries |

**Nothing was dropped.** One assertion was *deleted rather than re-spelled*, and it is worth naming: `ui/view.test.ts` read "Same file AND same line — one declaration reached by two import paths". The artifact carries no line, so the successor compares the origin strings, which is declaration identity — the thing the file+line pair was standing in for. Not a weakening; the pair could never distinguish two declarations that the origin string cannot.

### Why no line number, and why `node_modules` is normalised

Recording a line would rewrite this artifact on **every edit that shifts a line in any `.zod.ts`** — turning a comparison baseline into the repo's next merge-conflict magnet, which is the problem #5837 was solving, arriving from the other side. Same reasoning for the ten `./contracts` exports that resolve into `ai` / `@ai-sdk/provider-utils`: their real paths run through the pnpm store (`.pnpm/@ai-sdk+provider-utils@5.0.16_zod@4.4.3/…`), carrying a version and a peer-resolution hash, so everything up to the last `node_modules/` segment is dropped. Still an identity; stable across dependency bumps and across pnpm/npm layouts.

Sharded per entry point, following `api-surface/` and for its reason (#5837): retirement PRs rewrite whichever entries they touched, and the merge queue rebuilds server-side where no custom merge driver runs.

## Freshness — guarded twice, independently

A comparison is only as good as the thing compared, so this is the load-bearing half:

1. **`check:export-origins`** recomputes from source and byte-compares. Wired into `check:generated`'s `GATED` ledger **and** added as an explicit step in `lint.yml`'s required `TypeScript Type Check` job — a gate that exists but never runs is the dormant shape #4642 named. Reads `src/`, needs no build, ~3s.
2. **A compiler-free runtime cross-check** in the pins themselves: every origin whose kind survives to runtime must appear in the entry's real namespace object, and vice versa. So `pnpm test` alone is not blind to a doctored artifact. Type-only exports are erased at runtime and are covered by (1), which covers everything.

The generator also carries a `--self-test` (run ahead of `--check`) pinning the resolver's own two edges on a fixture: a re-export must read as **one** declaration, and two declarations sharing a name must **not**. A broken resolver would otherwise write a confidently wrong baseline that gate (1) would happily agree with.

## Reverse verification — predictions first, then runs

Predictions were written to disk before any probe ran.

### Probe A — hand-edit the artifact to claim a wrong origin

`export-origins/kernel.json`: `EventSchema` → `src/automation/state-machine.zod.ts#EventSchema (const)`.

| # | check | predicted | observed | ✓ |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| A1 | `check:export-origins` | RED | RED — `kernel.json is stale — the source resolves differently`, exit 1 | ✓ |
| A2 | `state-machine.test.ts` pin | RED | RED — `expected 'src/automation/state-machine.zod.ts' to be 'src/kernel/events/core.zod.ts'` | ✓ |
| A3 | runtime cross-check | **GREEN** (name set unchanged — the honest limit of guard 2) | GREEN | ✓ |

### Probe A′ — delete a runtime export from the artifact

`export-origins/automation.json`: drop `StateMachineSchema`.

| # | check | predicted | observed | ✓ |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| A′1 | `check:export-origins` | RED | RED, exit 1 | ✓ |
| A′2 | runtime cross-check, **no tsc** | RED | RED — `the module exports these at runtime and export-origins does not record them: expected [ 'StateMachineSchema' ] to deeply equal []` | ✓ |

A′ is the probe that proves guard 2 is not decoration: it fails on the real artifact with no compiler in the loop.

### Probe B — simulate the real regression the pin guards

Appended to `src/automation/index.ts`: `export { EventSchema } from '../kernel/events/core.zod';` — re-exporting the symbol #4658 retired, from a second entry point.

| # | check | predicted | observed | ✓ |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| B1 | pin, **stale** artifact | GREEN (pin cannot see it yet) | **RED** — the sibling runtime assertion `'EventSchema' in automation` caught it immediately | prediction **beaten** |
| B1′ | `check:export-origins`, stale artifact | RED | RED — `automation.json is stale`, exit 1 | ✓ |
| B2 | regenerate | `automation.json` gains `EventSchema` @ the kernel origin | `src/kernel/events/core.zod.ts#EventSchema (const)` | ✓ |
| B3 | pin, regenerated artifact | RED | RED — `expected [ …(239) ] to not include 'EventSchema'` **and** `expected true to be false` | ✓ |

B1 came out better than predicted and the row says so rather than being quietly re-worded: the family is red before regeneration as well as after, because each pin's runtime sibling is an independent witness. The sabotage was reverted and `check:export-origins` re-confirmed clean.

## The payoff, measured

Same 18 files, same container (4 vCPU), vitest JSON reporter, before = `origin/main`:

| | before | after |
|:--|--:|--:|
| wall clock | 31.8s | **11.2s** |
| aggregate test time | 76 315ms | **23 280ms** |
| the 17 pins | 55 455ms | **72ms** |
| tests run | 560 | 560 |

The 17 pins cost **0.13%** of what they did. The card measured ~39.0s over 12 files; on 18 files it had grown to 55.5s, exactly as "grows by one compilation per retirement PR" predicts — and the growth stops here, because a new pin now reads a baseline that is generated once.

What remains above 800ms in those files is module loading and the two class-B `createProgram` cases, not export-surface resolution.

## One collateral finding, and one config change

- **`src/kernel/activation-events-retirement.test.ts` graduated off the test-typecheck debt ledger.** Its single recorded error lived inside the compiler-API scaffolding this change removes. `check:test-typecheck` flagged it as a graduation and its entry is deleted in the same change, as that ratchet requires.
- **`tsconfig.test.json` widens `rootDir` to the package.** The testkit cannot live in `src/`: the BUILD config compiles every non-test `src/` file as CommonJS, where `import.meta` is TS1470, so a reader there could not resolve its own location. It lives in `scripts/lib/` beside the writer it mirrors — sharing its shard naming instead of restating it — and the only thing that blocked a `src` test from importing it was the emitting config's `rootDir` inherited into a **non-emitting** one. Under `noEmit` that setting has no output meaning; the program genuinely spans both directories already (`vitest.config.ts` runs `src/**/*.test.ts` *and* `scripts/**/*.test.ts`). `include` still stops at `src`, and no strictness moved — the file's header records all of this.
- `vitest.config.ts`'s `testTimeout` value is **left exactly where the stop-bleed put it**. Lowering it is a separate decision with its own measurement, and not this change's to make.

## Gates

Enumerated from `.github/workflows/lint.yml`, run one by one on the merged tree.

| gate | result |
|:--|:--|
| `pnpm lint` | ✅ |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` (`tsc` + scripts + test-typecheck) | ✅ |
| `check:generated` (all 11 artifacts) | ✅ |
| `check:generated --reconcile-only` | ✅ 20 `check:` + 14 `gen:`, all classified |
| `check:export-origins` (self-test + check) | ✅ |
| `check:api-surface` · `check:exported-any` · `check:dual-source-exports` | ✅ |
| `check:spec-changes` · `check:upgrade-guide` · `check:skill-docs` · `check:skill-refs` · `check:skill-examples` | ✅ |
| `check:merge-driver` · `check:shard-attestation` · `check:published-files` | ✅ |
| `check:type-check-coverage` · `check:stall-guard` · `check:adr-anchors` · `check:changeset-gate-self-tests` | ✅ |
| `node scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base origin/main` | ✅ nothing owed |
| `packages/spec` full suite | ✅ 355 files / 9 268 tests |

`check:react-declaration-parity` is the one gate that cannot run here (needs objectui's `sdui.manifest.json`); `check:generated` reports it as such rather than skipping.

`export-origins/` is deliberately **not** added to `package.json`'s `files` — it is a development baseline, unlike `api-surface/`, which release tooling unpacks from published tarballs.

## Concurrency

Merged `origin/main` (5 commits) after the work was complete; the merge was clean and `check:export-origins` confirmed the artifact still current — main's spec commits touched `filter.zod.ts` / `view.zod.ts` / `sharing-service.ts` but added no top-level exports. The pin family was **re-enumerated on the merged tree**: no new export-surface pins arrived. A generated-artifact conflict here resolves by regenerating from the merged tree, never by hand-merging; `.gitattributes` routes `export-origins/**` to `merge=os-regen` and `scripts/regen-artifacts.mjs` carries its `gen:`/`check:` pair, with `check:merge-driver` reconciling the two.

Not queued and not armed — landing is the PM's, serially.
